## Update a node

<a id="opIdput-node-balancer-node"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/nodebalancers/%7B%7BnodeBalancerId%7D%7D/configs/%7B%7BconfigId%7D%7D/nodes/%7B%7BnodeId%7D%7D \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": [
      "192.168.210.120:443",
      "10.100.5.5:80",
      "[2300:5800::f03c:93ff:fe6e:1264]:8080"
    ],
    "label": "node54321",
    "subnet_id": 1,
    "weight": 50
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/nodebalancers/{nodeBalancerId}/configs/{configId}/nodes/{nodeId}`

Updates information about a node, a backend for this NodeBalancer's configured port.

> 🚧
>
> You can configure UDP on the same NodeBalancer that also uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS, but only when managing it through the API. If UDP is configured and you make changes to the TCP, HTTP or HTTPS settings in Cloud Manager, the existing UDP configuration will be overwritten. This is because Cloud Manager doesn't currently support UDP.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI: TCP, HTTP, HTTPS__.

    ```
    linode-cli nodebalancers node-update \
  12345 4567 54321 \
  --address 192.168.210.120:80 \
  --label node54321 \
  --weight 50 \
  --mode accept
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __CLI: UDP__.

    ```
    linode-cli nodebalancers node-create \
  12345 4567 \
  --address 192.168.210.120:80 \
  --label node54321 \
  --weight 50
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    nodebalancers:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-node-balancer-node">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

```json

  "address": [
    "192.168.210.120:443",
    "10.100.5.5:80",
    "[2300:5800::f03c:93ff:fe6e:1264]:8080"
  ],
  "label": "node54321",
  "subnet_id": 1,
  "weight": 50
}
```

|weight|integer|false|none|Used when picking a backend to serve a request and is not pinned to a single backend yet. Nodes with a higher weight will receive more traffic.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|__Beta__ A NodeBalancer node represents a single backend serving requests for a single port of a NodeBalancer. Nodes are tied to individual NodeBalancer configurations and route traffic over their private IPv4 address, IPv6 address, or VPC IPv4 address.  If the same Linode is serving traffic for more than one port on the same NodeBalancer, one NodeBalancer node is required for each config (port) it should serve requests on.  For example, if you have four backends, and each should respond to both UDP and HTTPS requests, you will need two NodeBalancer configs (port 80 and port 443) and four backends each, one for each of the Linodes serving requests for that port.|
|address|string(ip)|false|none|The address and port where this backend can be reached: either the Linode’s private IPv4, public IPv6, or the VPC's IPv4 address.|
|config_id|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The NodeBalancer Config ID that this Node belongs to.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ This node's unique ID.|
|label|string|false|none|The label for this node.  This is for display purposes only.|
|mode|string|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The mode this NodeBalancer should use when sending traffic to this backend. For backend nodes with a UDP config, the `mode` doesn't apply, so the value is `none`.|
|nodebalancer_id|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The NodeBalancer ID that this Node belongs to.|
|status|string|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The current status of this node, based on the configured checks of its NodeBalancer config.|
|vpc_config_id|integer \| null|false|read-only|__Read-only__ For VPC backends, the `vpc_config_id` can be used to [get VPC IDs and VPC subnet IDs](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-node-balancer-vpc-config). Returns a `null` value if the backend is not a VPC node. Included only when the `apiVersion` is `v4beta`.|
|weight|integer|false|none|Used when picking a backend to serve a request and is not pinned to a single backend yet. Nodes with a higher weight will receive more traffic.|

## Delete a NodeBalancer's node

<a id="opIddelete-node-balancer-config-node"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/nodebalancers/%7B%7BnodeBalancerId%7D%7D/configs/%7B%7BconfigId%7D%7D/nodes/%7B%7BnodeId%7D%7D \

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/nodebalancers/{nodeBalancerId}/configs/{configId}/nodes/{nodeId}`

Deletes a Node from this Config. This backend will no longer receive traffic for the configured port of this NodeBalancer.

This does not change or remove the Linode whose address was used in the creation of this Node.

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-node-pools">Node pools</h1>

Create, manage, and configure node pools within your LKE clusters. Node pools allow you to group nodes with similar configurations and manage them collectively.

## List node pools

<a id="opIdget-lke-cluster-pools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/lke/clusters/%7B%7BclusterId%7D%7D/pools \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools`

## Create a node pool

<a id="opIdpost-lke-cluster-pools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/lke/clusters/%7B%7BclusterId%7D%7D/pools \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoscaler": {
      "enabled": true,
      "max": 12,
      "min": 3
    },
    "count": 6,
    "disk_encryption": "enabled",
    "disks": [
      {
        "size": 1024,
        "type": "ext4"
      }
    ],
    "k8s_version": "v1.31.8+lke3",
    "label": "app-pool",
    "labels": {
      "example.com/my-app": "teams"
    },
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ],
    "taints": [
      {
        "effect": "NoSchedule",
        "key": "example.com/my-app",
        "value": "teamA"
      },
      {
        "effect": "NoExecute",
        "key": "myapp.io/team",
        "value": "teamB"
      }
    ],
    "type": "g6-standard-4",
    "update_strategy": "on_recycle"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools`

Creates a new Node Pool for the designated Kubernetes cluster.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli lke pool-create 12345 \
  --type g6-standard-4 \
  --count 6 \
  --tags example-tag \
  --autoscaler.enabled true \
  --autoscaler.max 12 \
  --autoscaler.min 3 \
  --labels '{ "example.com/my-app":"team1" }' \
  --taints.effect "NoSchedule" \
  --taints.key "example.com/my-app" \
  --taints.value "teamA"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    lke:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-lke-cluster-pools">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

{
  "autoscaler": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max": 12,
    "min": 3
  },
  "count": 6,
  "disk_encryption": "enabled",

    {
      "size": 1024,
      "type": "ext4"
    }
  ],
  "k8s_version": "v1.31.8+lke3",
  "label": "app-pool",
  "labels": {
    "example.com/my-app": "teams"
  },

    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],

    {
      "effect": "NoSchedule",
      "key": "example.com/my-app",
      "value": "teamA"
    },
    {
      "effect": "NoExecute",
      "key": "myapp.io/team",
      "value": "teamB"
    }
  ],
  "type": "g6-standard-4",
  "update_strategy": "on_recycle"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-node-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster to look up.|
|body|body|object|true|Configuration for the Node Pool.|
|» autoscaler|body|object|false|When enabled, the number of nodes automatically scales within the defined minimum and maximum values. When making a request, `max` and `min` require each other.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic scaling is enabled for this node pool. Defaults to `false`.|
|» » max|body|integer|false|The maximum number of nodes to automatically scale to. Defaults to the value provided by the `count` field.|
|» » min|body|integer|false|The minimum number of nodes to automatically scale to. Defaults to the node pool's `count`.|
|» count|body|integer|true|The number of nodes in the node pool.|
|» disk_encryption|body|string|false|Local disk encryption setting for this LKE node pool. Defaults to `disabled`.|
|» disks|body|[object]|false|This node pool's custom disk layout. Each item in this array will create a new disk partition for each node in this node pool.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> Omit this field, except for special use cases. The disks specified here are partitions in _addition_ to the primary partition and reduce the size of the primary partition. This can lead to stability problems for the node.<br><br>  - The custom disk layout is applied to each node in this node pool.<br><br>  - The maximum number of custom disk partitions that can be configured is 7.<br><br>  - Once the requested disk partitions are allocated, the remaining disk space is allocated to the node's boot disk.<br><br>  - A node pool's custom disk layout is immutable over the lifetime of the node pool.|
|» » size|body|integer|false|The size of this custom disk partition in MB. The size of this disk partition can't exceed the capacity of the node's plan type.|
|» » type|body|string|false|This custom disk partition's filesystem type.|
|» k8s_version|body|string|false|__Beta__, __LKE Enterprise__ The LKE-specific Kubernetes version to use for the worker nodes within this node pool. This field is required when creating node pools on LKE Enterprise clusters.<br><br>> 🚧<br>><br>> This field is available as part of the beta API and can only be used with accounts that have been enrolled in the LKE Enterprise LA. Call the URL with the `apiVersion` path parameter set to `v4beta`.|
|» label|body|string|false|__Beta__ An optional label for this node pool. Labels can be up to 32 characters long, containing lowercase alphanumeric characters optionally interspersed with dashes.<br><br>A node pool's label also cascades down to its nodes (Linodes). If a label is defined on the node pool, the label for each node is `<cluster-id>-<nodepool-label>-<hash>`. If not, the label is `<cluster-id>-<nodepool-id>-<hash>`.<br><br>> 🚧<br>><br>> This field is available as part of the beta API and can only be used with accounts that have been enrolled in the LKE Enterprise LA. Call the URL with the `apiVersion` path parameter set to `v4beta`.|
|» labels|body|object|false|Key-value pairs added as labels to nodes in the node pool. Labels help classify your nodes and easily select subsets of objects. To learn more, review [Add Labels and Taints to your LKE node pools](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/compute/kubernetes/guides/deploy-and-manage-cluster-with-the-linode-api/#add-labels-and-taints-to-your-lke-node-pools).<br><br>**Label key:**<br><br>- A key can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- If the key begins with a DNS subdomain prefix followed by a single slash, for example `example.com/my-app`, the maximum total length of the label key is 128 characters. Domain labels can be up to 62 characters after the '/'. The prefix needs to adhere to [RFC 1123](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1123) DNS subdomain restrictions.<br><br>- If the key doesn't begin with a DNS subdomain prefix, the maximum key length is 63 characters.<br><br>Specifying an empty object removes all previously set labels.<br><br>**Label value:**<br><br>- The label's value can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- Can be specified as an empty string value with `""`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|__Filterable__ Organizational tags to apply to this node pool. When you apply tags to LKE Enterprise node pools, they also apply to the nodes (Linodes) within the node pool. Tags don't cascade down to nodes in non-Enterprise node pools.|
|» taints|body|[object]|false|Kubernetes taints to add to node pool nodes. Taints help control how pods are scheduled onto nodes, specifically allowing them to repel certain pods. To learn more, review [Add labels and taints to your LKE node pools](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/compute/kubernetes/guides/deploy-and-manage-cluster-with-the-linode-api/#add-labels-and-taints-to-your-lke-node-pools).<br><br>Specifying an empty array (`[]`) removes all previously set taints.|
|» » effect|body|string|true|The Kubernetes taint effect. For `NoSchedule`, `PreferNoSchedule` and `NoExecute` descriptions, see [Kubernetes Taints and Tolerations](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/).|
|» » key|body|string|true|The Kubernetes taint key.<br><br>- A key can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- If the key begins with a DNS subdomain prefix followed by a single slash, for example `example.com/my-app`, the prefix part needs to adhere to [RFC 1123](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1123) DNS subdomain restrictions and be a maximum of 253 characters.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The Kubernetes taint value.<br><br>- A key can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- Can be specified as an empty string value with `""`.|
|» type|body|string|true|The Linode Type for all of the nodes in the node pool.|
|» update_strategy|body|string|false|__Beta__, __LKE Enterprise__ Determines when the worker nodes within this node pool upgrade to the latest selected Kubernetes version, after the cluster has been upgraded. This field is required when creating node pools on LKE Enterprise clusters.<br><br>- `rolling_update`: Immediately triggers a recycle of this node pool when the Kubernetes version is updated.<br>- `on_recycle` (default): Does not trigger any immediate recycle. New worker nodes are created with the new Kubernetes version. Existing worker nodes will be upgraded when a recycle is manually triggered.<br><br>> 🚧<br>><br>> This field is available as part of the beta API and can only be used with accounts that have been enrolled in the LKE Enterprise LA. Call the URL with the `apiVersion` path parameter set to `v4beta`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|
|» disk_encryption|enabled|

## Update a node pool

<a id="opIdput-lke-node-pool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/lke/clusters/%7B%7BclusterId%7D%7D/pools/%7B%7BpoolId%7D%7D \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoscaler": {
      "enabled": true,
      "max": 12,
      "min": 3
    },
    "count": "{{count}}",
    "labels": {
      "example.com/my-app": "teams"
    },
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ],
    "taints": [
      {
        "effect": "NoSchedule",
        "key": "example.com/my-app",
        "value": "teamA"
      },
      {
        "effect": "NoExecute",
        "key": "myapp.io/team",
        "value": "teamB"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools/{poolId}`

Updates a node pool's count, labels and taints, and autoscaler configuration.

Linodes are created or deleted to match changes to the Node Pool's count.

Specifying labels or taints on update overwrites any previous values, and updates existing nodes with the new values without a recycle.

__Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as `hostPath` and `emptyDir` volumes, or `local` PersistentVolumes) will be erased.__


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli lke pool-update 12345 456 \
  --count 6 \
  --autoscaler.enabled true \
  --autoscaler.max 12 \
  --autoscaler.min 3 \
  --labels '{ "example.com/my-app":"team1", "env":"staging" }' \
  --taints.effect "NoSchedule" \
  --taints.key "example.com/my-app" \
  --taints.value "teamA"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    lke:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-lke-node-pool">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoscaler": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max": 12,
    "min": 3
  },
  "count": "{{count}}",
  "labels": {
    "example.com/my-app": "teams"
  },
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "taints": [
    {
      "effect": "NoSchedule",
      "key": "example.com/my-app",
      "value": "teamA"
    },
    {
      "effect": "NoExecute",
      "key": "myapp.io/team",
      "value": "teamB"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-node-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster to look up.|
|poolId|path|integer|true|ID of the Pool to look up.|
|body|body|object|false|The fields to update.|
|» autoscaler|body|object|false|When enabled, the number of nodes automatically scales within the defined minimum and maximum values. When making a request, `max` and `min` require each other.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic scaling is enabled for this node pool. Defaults to `false`.|
|» » max|body|integer|false|The maximum number of nodes to automatically scale to. Defaults to the value provided by the `count` field.|
|» » min|body|integer|false|The minimum number of nodes to automatically scale to. Defaults to the node pool's `count`.|
|» count|body|integer|false|The number of nodes in the node pool.|
|» labels|body|object|false|Key-value pairs added as labels to nodes in the node pool. Labels help classify your nodes and easily select subsets of objects. To learn more, review [Add Labels and Taints to your LKE node pools](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/compute/kubernetes/guides/deploy-and-manage-cluster-with-the-linode-api/#add-labels-and-taints-to-your-lke-node-pools).<br><br>**Label key:**<br><br>- A key can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- If the key begins with a DNS subdomain prefix followed by a single slash, for example `example.com/my-app`, the maximum total length of the label key is 128 characters. Domain labels can be up to 62 characters after the '/'. The prefix needs to adhere to [RFC 1123](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1123) DNS subdomain restrictions.<br><br>- If the key doesn't begin with a DNS subdomain prefix, the maximum key length is 63 characters.<br><br>Specifying an empty object removes all previously set labels.<br><br>**Label value:**<br><br>- The label's value can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- Can be specified as an empty string value with `""`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|__Filterable__ Organizational tags to apply to this node pool. When you apply tags to LKE Enterprise node pools, they also apply to the nodes (Linodes) within the node pool. Tags don't cascade down to nodes in non-Enterprise node pools.|
|» taints|body|[object]|false|Kubernetes taints to add to node pool nodes. Taints help control how pods are scheduled onto nodes, specifically allowing them to repel certain pods. To learn more, review [Add labels and taints to your LKE node pools](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/compute/kubernetes/guides/deploy-and-manage-cluster-with-the-linode-api/#add-labels-and-taints-to-your-lke-node-pools).<br><br>Specifying an empty array (`[]`) removes all previously set taints.|
|» » effect|body|string|true|The Kubernetes taint effect. For `NoSchedule`, `PreferNoSchedule` and `NoExecute` descriptions, see [Kubernetes Taints and Tolerations](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/).|
|» » key|body|string|true|The Kubernetes taint key.<br><br>- A key can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- If the key begins with a DNS subdomain prefix followed by a single slash, for example `example.com/my-app`, the prefix part needs to adhere to [RFC 1123](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1123) DNS subdomain restrictions and be a maximum of 253 characters.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The Kubernetes taint value.<br><br>- A key can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), or dots (`.`). Start and end it with an alphanumeric character.<br><br>- Can be specified as an empty string value with `""`.|

|» status|not_ready|
|» effect|NoSchedule|
|» effect|PreferNoSchedule|
|» effect|NoExecute|

## Delete a node pool

<a id="opIddelete-lke-node-pool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/lke/clusters/%7B%7BclusterId%7D%7D/pools/%7B%7BpoolId%7D%7D \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools/{poolId}`

Delete a specific Node Pool from a Kubernetes cluster.

__Deleting a Node Pool is a destructive action and cannot be undone.__

Deleting a Node Pool will delete all Linodes within that Pool.

## Recycle a node pool

<a id="opIdpost-lke-cluster-pool-recycle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/lke/clusters/%7B%7BclusterId%7D%7D/pools/%7B%7BpoolId%7D%7D/recycle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools/{poolId}/recycle`

Recycles a Node Pool for the designated Kubernetes Cluster. All Linodes within the Node Pool will be deleted and replaced with new Linodes on a rolling basis, which may take several minutes. Replacement Nodes are installed with the latest available patch for the Cluster's Kubernetes Version.

__Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as `hostPath` and `emptyDir` volumes, or `local` PersistentVolumes) will be erased.__


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli lke pool-recycle 12345 456
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    lke:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-lke-cluster-pool-recycle">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-lke-service-tokens">LKE service tokens</h1>

Regenerate service account tokens for your LKE clusters, which are used by the cluster's control plane components and Linode CSI drivers to authenticate with the Kubernetes API server.

## Delete a service token

<a id="opIddelete-lke-service-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/lke/clusters/%7B%7BclusterId%7D%7D/servicetoken \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/lke/clusters/{clusterId}/servicetoken`

Delete and regenerate the service account token for a Cluster.

> 📘
>
> When you regenerate a service account token, the cluster's control plane components and Linode CSI drivers are also restarted and configured with the new token. High availability clusters shouldn't experience any disruption, while standard clusters may experience brief control plane downtime while components are restarted.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli lke service-token-delete 12345
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    lke:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

## Delete a Longview client

<a id="opIddelete-longview-client"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/longview/clients/%7B%7BclientId%7D%7D \

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/longview/clients/{clientId}`

__All information stored for this client will be lost.__

This _does not_ uninstall the Longview Client application for your Linode - you must do that manually.

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-longview-plans">Longview plans</h1>

Get details on your current Longview plan subscription and, if needed, update your plan.

## Get a Longview plan

<a id="opIdget-longview-plan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/longview/plan \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/longview/plan`

Get the details of your current Longview plan. This returns a `LongviewSubscription` object for your current Longview Pro plan, or an empty set `{}` if your current plan is Longview Free.

You must have at least one of the following `global` [List a user's grants](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-user-grants) in order to run this operation:

  - `"account_access": read_write`
  - `"account_access": read_only`
  - `"longview_subscription": true`
  - `"add_longview": true`

To update your subscription plan, send a request to [Update a Longview plan](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-longview-plan).


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli longview plan-view
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    longview:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

  }
}

## Update a Longview plan

<a id="opIdput-longview-plan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/longview/plan \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "longview_subscription": "{{longview_subscription}}"
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/longview/plan`

Update your Longview plan to that of the given subscription ID. This returns a `LongviewSubscription` object for the updated Longview Pro plan, or an empty set `{}` if the updated plan is Longview Free.

You must have `"longview_subscription": true` configured as a `global` [user grant](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-user-grants) in order to run this operation.

You can send a request to the [List Longview subscriptions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-longview-subscriptions) operation to receive the details, including `id`'s, of each plan.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli longview plan-update --longview_subscription longview-10
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    longview:read_write
    ```

## Create a managed credential

<a id="opIdpost-managed-credential"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/managed/credentials \

## Create a managed service

<a id="opIdpost-managed-service"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/managed/services \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "https://example.org",
    "body": "it worked",
    "consultation_group": "on-call",
    "credentials": [
      9991
    ],
    "label": "prod-1",
    "notes": "The service name is my-cool-application",
    "region": null,
    "service_type": "url",
    "timeout": 30
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/managed/services`

Creates a service monitor. Linode Managed monitors this service and alerts Akamai Support when issues are detected.

This operation can only be accessed by the unrestricted users of an account.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli managed service-create \
  --service_type url \
  --label prod-1 \
  --address "https://example.org" \
  --timeout 30 \
  --body "it worked" \
  --consultation_group on-call \
  --notes "The service name is \
    my-cool-application" \
  --credentials 9991
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-managed-service">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

  "address": "https://example.org",
  "body": "it worked",
  "consultation_group": "on-call",
  "credentials": [
    9991
  ],
  "label": "prod-1",
  "notes": "The service name is my-cool-application",
  "region": null,
  "service_type": "url",
  "timeout": 30
}
```

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-managed-statistics">Managed statistics</h1>

View key metrics for your managed Linodes, including CPU usage, disk I/O, and network transfer.

## List managed stats

<a id="opIdget-managed-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/managed/stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/managed/stats`

Returns a list of metrics for the Linodes on your account in arrays of coordinates (_x_-axis and _y_-axis data points). You can use these data points to plot your own graph visualizations. These metrics reflect the last 24 hours of combined usage across all managed Linodes on your account, giving you a high-level snapshot of data for the following:

- CPU
- Disk I/O
- Swap usage
- Network in
- Network out

This operation can only be accessed by the unrestricted users of an account.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli managed stats-list
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-metrics">Metrics</h1>

## Get an entity's metrics

<a id="opIdpost-read-metric"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/monitor/services/%7B%7BserviceType%7D%7D/metrics \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "absolute_time_duration": {
      "end": "2024-10-16T02:00:00Z",
      "start": "2024-10-14T01:00:00Z"
    },
    "entity_ids": [
      13116,
      13217,
      13331
    ],
    "filters": [
      {
        "dimension_label": "node_type",
        "operator": "eq",
        "value": "primary"
      }
    ],
    "group_by": [
      "entity_id",
      "node_type"
    ],
    "metrics": [
      {
        "aggregate_function": "avg",
        "name": "read_iops"
      },
      {
        "aggregate_function": "avg",
        "name": "cpu_usage"
      }
    ],
    "time_granularity": {
      "unit": "sec",
      "value": 700
    }
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/monitor/services/{serviceType}/metrics`

__Beta__ Returns metrics information for the individual entities within a specific service type. Thi operation also requires an `authorization: Bearer` [token](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-get-token) you've created for this `serviceType`.

> 📘
>
> - This operation uses a different URL and version from standard Linode API operations. Verify you're using the URL with the `monitor-api.linode.com` hostname and include `v2beta` as the version in the URL.
>
> - For more details on the metrics available for each service, see the [Metrics reference](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/metrics-dimensions-parameters).

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-read-metric">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

## Create a token for a service type

<a id="opIdpost-get-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/monitor/services/%7B%7BserviceType%7D%7D/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ref": "../examples/post-aclp-token-request-200.json"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/monitor/services/{serviceType}/token`

__Beta__ Returns a token that authenticates requests for the entities within a specific service type. The token has a lifetime of six hours after you create it. For an example of the token generation process, see [Authenticate Monitor API operations](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#authenticate-monitor-api-operations).

> 📘
>
> - This operation is beta. Call it using the `v4beta` path in its URL.
>
> - To see your currently supported services, run the [List supported service types](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-monitor-services) operation.
>
> - You also need `read_only` access to the [scope](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth-reference) for the specified `serviceType`.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli monitor token-get dbaas \
--entity_ids 189690 \
--entity_ids 188020 --json
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    monitor:read_only, <service_type>:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-get-token">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ref": "../examples/post-aclp-token-request-200.json"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-token-for-a-service-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call the `v4beta` URL for operations still only in beta.|
|serviceType|path|string|true|The Akamai Cloud Computing service being monitored. To see your currently supported services, run the [List supported service types](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-monitor-services) operation and store the appropriate `service_type`.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» entity_ids|body|[integer]|true|The `id` for each individual entity from a `service_type`. Get this value by running the list operation for the appropriate entity. For example, if your entity is one of your PostgreSQL databases, run the [List PostgreSQL Managed Databases](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-databases-postgre-sql-instances) operation and store the `id` for the appropriate database from the response.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> - This field is required and supports up to 100 total entries.<br>><br>> - You need read access permission to all of the entities you include in the token. Run the [List a user's grants](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-user-grants) operation to see the permission level for each entity in your account.|

}

In most cases, this can be fixed immediately by changing the data you sent in the request, but in some cases you will be instructed to [Open a support ticket](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-ticket) or perform some other action before you can complete the request successfully.|

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-alerts">Alerts</h1>

Akamai Cloud Pulse lets you configure alerts to monitor key metrics and events in real time and automatically trigger notifications or actions when predefined thresholds or conditions are met.

## List alert channels

<a id="opIdget-alert-channels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/monitor/alert-channels \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/monitor/alert-channels`

__Beta__ Returns all of the monitoring alert channels available to your user.

> 📘
>
> - This operation is beta. Call it using the `v4beta` path in its URL.
>
> - [Filtering](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/filtering-and-sorting) is supported for specific objects, labeled as **Filterable**. However, only the `+and` and `+or` operators are supported, and you can't nest filter operators.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    monitor:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli alerts channels-list
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-alert-channels">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

`GET /{apiVersion}/monitor/alert-definitions`

__Beta__ Returns all available alert definitions on your account.

> 📘
>

<h3 id="list-alert-definitions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|false|none|none|
|» alert_channels|[object]|false|none|The alert channels set up for use with this alert. Run the [List alert channels](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-alert-channels) operation to see all of the available channels.|
|» » id|integer|false|none|The unique identifier for this alert channel on your account.|
|» » label|string|false|none|The name of the channel, used to display it in Akamai Cloud Manager.|
|» » type|string|false|none|The type of notification used with the channel. For a `user` alert definition, only `email` is supported.|
|» » url|string(url)|false|none|The URL for the channel that ends in the channel's `id`.|
|» class|string \| null|false|none|The plan type for the Managed Database cluster, either `shared` or `dedicated`. This only applies to a `system` alert for a `service_type` of `dbaas` (Managed Databases). For `user` alerts for `dbaas`, this is returned as `null`.|
|» created|string(date-time)|false|none|When the alert definition was created.|
|» created_by|string|false|none|For a `user` alert definition, this is the user on your account that [created](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-alert-definition-for-service-type) it. For a `system` alert definition, this is returned as `system`.|
|» description|string|false|none|An additional description for the alert definition.|
|» entity_ids|[string]|false|none|The `id` for each individual entity from a `service_type`. Get this value by running the list operation for the appropriate entity. For example, if your entity is one of your PostgreSQL databases, run the [List PostgreSQL Managed Databases](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-databases-postgre-sql-instances) operation and store the `id` for the appropriate database from the response.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> The format `type` for an `entity_id` may vary, based on the Akamai Cloud `service_type`. For example, the `dbaas` service returns an integer value for an `id`, that you'd use for the `entity_id`. Other services may return a string for their `id`. With the Alerts operations, all of these formats are recognized as an `entity_id`, when you include them as a `string`.|
|» has_more_resources|boolean|false|none|Whether there are additional `entity_ids` associated with the alert for which the user doesn't have at least `read-only` access.|
|» id|integer|false|none|__Filterable__ The unique identifier for the alert definition.|
|» label|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The name of the alert definition. This is used for display purposes in Akamai Cloud Manager.|
|» rule_criteria|object|false|none|Details for the rules required to trigger the alert.|
|» » rules|[object]|false|none|The individual rules that make up the alert definition.|
|» » » aggregate_function|string|false|none|The aggregation function applied to the `metric`. Available values are `avg`, `sum`, `min`, and `max`.|
|» » » dimension_filters|[object]|false|none|Dimension filters for the rule.|
|» » » » dimension_label|string|false|none|The name of the dimension to be used in the filter.|
|» » » » label|string|false|none|The name of the dimension filter. Used for display purposes.|
|» » » » operator|string|false|none|The operator to apply to the dimension filter. Available values are `eq` for equal, `neq` for not equal, `startswith`, and `endswith`.|
|» » » » value|string|false|none|The value to compare the `dimension_label` against.|
|» » » label|string|false|none|The name of the individual rule. This is used for display purposes in Akamai Cloud Manager.|
|» » » metric|string|false|none|The metric to query.|
|» » » operator|string|false|none|The operator to apply to the metric. Available values are `eq` for equal, `gt` for greater than, `lt` for less than, `gte` for greater than or equal, and `lte` for less than or equal.|
|» » » threshold|number(float)|false|none|The predefined value or condition that triggers an alert when met or exceeded. For example, for `avg(cpu_usage) > 80`, the `threshold` is 80.|
|» » » unit|string|false|none|The unit of the metric. This can be values like `percent` for percentage or `GB` for gigabyte.|
|» service_type|string|false|none|The identifier for the Akamai Cloud Computing service. Use this value to call out the service in other Monitor operations in the API.|
|» severity|integer|false|none|The severity of the alert. Supported values include `3` for info, `2` for low, `1` for medium, and `0` for severe.|
|» status|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The current status of the alert. This can be either `enabled`, `disabled`, `in progress`, or `failed`.|
|» trigger_conditions|object|false|none|The conditions that need to be met to send a notification for the alert.|
|» » criteria_condition|string|false|none|Signifies the logical operation applied when multiple metrics are set for an alert definition. For example, if you wanted to apply both `cpu_usage > 90` and `memory_usage > 80`, `ALL` is the `criteria_condition`.  Currently, only `ALL` is supported.|
|» » evaluation_period_seconds|integer|false|none|The time period over which data is collected before evaluating whether the alert definition's `threshold` has been met or exceeded.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> During the beta, only a value of `300` seconds is supported.|
|» » polling_interval_seconds|integer|false|none|The frequency at which the `metric` is checked for a change in state. For example, with `cpu_usage` set as your `metric` and this set to `300`, your `cpu_usage` is checked every 5 minutes for some change in its state.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> During the beta, only a value of `300` seconds is supported.|
|» » trigger_occurrences|integer|false|none|The minimum number of consecutive `polling_interval_seconds` periods that the `threshold` needs to be breached to trigger the alert.|
|» type|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The type of alert. This can be either `user` for an alert specific to the current user, or `system` for one that applies to all users on your account.|
|» updated|string(date-time)|false|none|When the alert definition was last updated. This is the same as `created` if the alert definition hasn't been updated.|
|» updated_by|string|false|none|For a `user` alert definition, this is the user on your account that last [updated](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-alert-definition) it. For a `system` alert definition, this is returned as `system`. If it hasn't been updated, this value is the same as `created_by`.|
|page|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The current [page](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/pagination).|
|pages|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The total number of [pages](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/pagination).|
|results|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The total number of results.|

## List alert definitions for a service type

<a id="opIdget-alert-definitions-for-service-type"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/monitor/services/%7B%7BserviceType%7D%7D/alert-definitions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/monitor/services/{serviceType}/alert-definitions`

__Beta__ Returns all available alert definitions for a specific service type.

> 📘
>
> This operation is beta. Call it using the `v4beta` path in its URL.

## Create an alert definition

<a id="opIdpost-alert-definition-for-service-type"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/monitor/services/%7B%7BserviceType%7D%7D/alert-definitions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "channel_ids": [
      546,
      392
    ],
    "description": "Alert for my PostgreSQL database.",
    "entity_ids": [
      "13116",
      "13217",
      "13331"
    ],
    "label": "High Memory Usage Plan Dedicated",
    "rule_criteria": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "aggregate_function": "min",
          "dimension_filters": [
            {
              "dimension_label": "node_type",
              "operator": "eq",
              "value": "primary"
            }
          ],
          "label": "CPU Usage",
          "metric": "cpu_usage",
          "operator": "gt",
          "threshold": 80
        }
      ]
    },
    "severity": 1,
    "trigger_conditions": {
      "criteria_condition": "ALL",
      "evaluation_period_seconds": 300,
      "polling_interval_seconds": 300,
      "trigger_occurrences": 3
    }
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/monitor/services/{serviceType}/alert-definitions`

__Beta__ Create a new alert definition for a specific service type. Akamai refers to these as `user` alerts. You need `read_only` access to the [scope](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth-reference) for the selected `serviceType`. Check out this [workflow](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/create-a-logs-stream) for the basics on set up of a destination and a stream to gather logs.

> 📘
>
> This operation is beta. Call it using the `v4beta` path in its URL.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    monitor:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli alerts definition-create \
--channel_ids 546 \
--label CPU usage threshold maximum \
--rule_criteria.metric cpu_usage \
--rule_criteria.operator gt \
--rule_criteria.threshold 80 \
--severity 2
--trigger_conditions.evaluation_period_seconds 300 \
--trigger_conditions.polling_interval_seconds 300 \
--trigger_conditions.trigger_occurrences 3 \
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-alert-definition-for-service-type">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

<h3 id="create-an-alert-definition-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call the `v4beta` URL for operations still only in beta.|
|serviceType|path|string|true|The Akamai Cloud Computing service being monitored. To see your currently supported services, run the [List supported service types](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-monitor-services) operation and store the appropriate `service_type`.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» channel_ids|body|[integer]|true|The identifiers for the alert channels to use for the alert. Run the [List alert channels](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-alert-channels) operation and store the `id` for the applicable channels.|
|» description|body|string|false|An additional description for the alert definition.|
|» entity_ids|body|[string]|false|The `id` for each individual entity from a `service_type`. Get this value by running the list operation for the appropriate entity. For example, if your entity is one of your PostgreSQL databases, run the [List PostgreSQL Managed Databases](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-databases-postgre-sql-instances) operation and store the `id` for the appropriate database from the response. You also need `read_only` access to the [scope](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth-reference) for the `service_type` for each of the `entity_ids`.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> The format `type` for an `entity_id` may vary, based on the Akamai Cloud `service_type`. For example, the `dbaas` service returns an integer value for an `id`, that you'd use for the `entity_id`, while other services may return a string for their `id`. With the Alerts operations, all of these formats are recognized as an `entity_id`, when you include them as a `string`.|
|» label|body|string|true|The name of the alert definition. This is used for display purposes in Akamai Cloud Manager.|
|» rule_criteria|body|object|true|Details for the rules required to trigger the alert.|
|» » rules|body|[object]|false|The individual rules that make up the alert definition.|
|» » » aggregate_function|body|string|false|The aggregation function applied to the `metric`. Available values are `avg`, `sum`, `min`, and `max`.|
|» » » dimension_filters|body|[object]|false|Individual objects that define dimension filters for the rule.|
|» » » » dimension_label|body|string|false|The name of the dimension to be used in the filter.|
|» » » » operator|body|string|false|The operator to apply to the dimension filter. Available values are `eq` for equal, `neq` for not equal, `startswith`, and `endswith`.|
|» » » » value|body|string|false|The value to compare the `dimension_label` against.|
|» » » metric|body|string|false|The metric to query.|
|» » » operator|body|string|false|The operator to apply to the metric. Available values are `eq` for equal, `gt` for greater than, `lt` for less than `gte` for greater than or equal, and `lte` for less than or equal.|
|» » » threshold|body|number(float)|false|The predefined value or condition that triggers an alert when met or exceeded. For example, for `avg(cpu_usage) > 80`, the `threshold` is 80.|
|» severity|body|integer|true|The severity of the alert. Supported values include `3` for info, `2` for low, `1` for medium, and `0` for severe.|
|» trigger_conditions|body|object|true|The conditions that need to be met to send a notification for the alert.|
|» » criteria_condition|body|string|false|Signifies the logical operation applied when multiple metrics are set for an alert definition. For example, if you wanted to apply both `cpu_usage > 90` and `memory_usage > 80`, `ALL` is the `criteria_condition`. Currently, only `ALL` is supported.|
|» » evaluation_period_seconds|body|integer|false|The time period over which data is collected before evaluating whether the alert definition's `threshold` has been met or exceeded.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> During the beta, only a value of `300` seconds is supported.|
|» » polling_interval_seconds|body|integer|false|The frequency at which the `metric` is checked for a change in state. For example, with `cpu_usage` set as your `metric` and this set to `300`, your `cpu_usage` is checked every 5 minutes for some change in its state.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> During the beta, only a value of `300` seconds is supported.|
|» » trigger_occurrences|body|integer|false|The minimum number of consecutive `polling_interval_seconds` periods that the `threshold` needs to be breached to trigger the alert.|

## Update an alert definition

<a id="opIdput-alert-definition"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/monitor/services/%7B%7BserviceType%7D%7D/alert-definitions/%7B%7BalertId%7D%7D \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "channel_ids": [
      546,
      392
    ],
    "description": "Alert for my PostgreSQL database.",
    "entity_ids": [
      "13116",
      "13217",
      "13331"
    ],
    "label": "High Memory Usage Plan Dedicated",
    "rule_criteria": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "aggregate_function": "min",
          "dimension_filters": [
            {
              "dimension_label": "node_type",
              "operator": "eq",
              "value": "primary"
            }
          ],
          "label": "CPU Usage",
          "metric": "cpu_usage",
          "operator": "gt",
          "threshold": 80
        }
      ]
    },
    "severity": 1,
    "status": "enabled",
    "trigger_conditions": {
      "criteria_condition": "ALL",
      "evaluation_period_seconds": 300,
      "polling_interval_seconds": 300,
      "trigger_occurrences": 3
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/monitor/services/{serviceType}/alert-definitions/{alertId}`

__Beta__ Update an existing alert definition. You need `read_only` access to the [scope](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth-reference) for the selected `serviceType`. Only include the objects in the request that you want to update. Leave any object out of the request to leave it set as is.

> 📘
>
> This operation is beta. Call it using the `v4beta` path in its URL.

**User alert definitions**

When updating an alert definition you've [created](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-alert-definition-for-service-type), you can change the `status` to `enabled` or `disabled`. You can also modify the `label`, `description`, `severity`, `entity_ids`, `rule_criteria`, `trigger_conditions`, and `channel_ids` objects. If updating the `entity_ids`, `rule_criteria`, or `channel_ids` list objects, these points apply:

- If you want to keep an existing item, you need to include it in the list.

- If you want to remove an existing item, leave it out of the list.

- To add a new item, include it in the list.

- You can't pass an empty list to remove all items. This doesn't apply to the `entity_ids` or `dimension_filters` (in `rule_criteria`) list objects, because they are optional, while all other list objects are required.

**System alert definitions**

These are the default alert definitions offered by Akamai. You can only edit the `entity_ids` list object for these alerts. All of the points above regarding editing a list object apply here, too.

## Delete an alert definition

<a id="opIddelete-alert-definition"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/monitor/services/{serviceType}/alert-definitions/{alertId}`

__Beta__ Delete a specific alert definition on your account.

> 📘

> - An [alert definition](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-alert-definitions) with a `type` of `system` can't be deleted.

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-buckets">Buckets</h1>

Buckets are the primary containers within Object Storage. Each bucket stores your files (objects) and lets you access or share those files. Use these operations to create and manage buckets, as well as the objects in them.

## List Object Storage buckets

<a id="opIdget-object-storage-buckets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets`

Returns a paginated list of all Object Storage buckets available in your account.

> 📘
>
> You can use an outside API, such as the [Ceph Object Gateway S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/serviceops/#list-buckets) for more options.

## Create an Object Storage bucket

<a id="opIdpost-object-storage-bucket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "acl": "{{acl}}",
    "cors_enabled": "{{cors_enabled}}",
    "endpoint_type": "{{endpoint_type}}",
    "label": "{{label}}",
    "region": "{{region}}",
    "s3_endpoint": "{{s3_endpoint}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets`

Creates an Object Storage bucket in the specified data center ([region](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-regions)). If the bucket already exists on your account, this operation returns a 200 response with that bucket as if the API just created it.

> 📘
>
> - Accounts with negative balances can't access this operation.
>
> - The API still supports the `clusterId` equivalent (`us-west-1`) when setting a `region` for a new bucket, but you should use the `regionId` (`us-west`) instead.
>
> - This operation has specific [rate limits](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/rate-limits#specific-operation-rate-limits).
>
> - You can use an outside API, such as the [Ceph Object Gateway S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/bucketops/#put-bucket) for more options.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    object_storage:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-bucket">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acl": "{{acl}}",
  "cors_enabled": "{{cors_enabled}}",
  "endpoint_type": "{{endpoint_type}}",
  "label": "{{label}}",
  "region": "{{region}}",
  "s3_endpoint": "{{s3_endpoint}}"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-object-storage-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|body|body|object|false|Information about the bucket you want to create.|
|» acl|body|string|false|The S3 predefined collection of grantees and permissions set for the bucket, also referred to as a [Canned ACL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/acl-overview.html#canned-acl).|
|» cors_enabled|body|boolean|false|If set to `false`, cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) is disabled for all origins in the bucket.|
|» endpoint_type|body|string|false|The type of `s3_endpoint` available to the active `user` in this `region`. See [Endpoint types](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/object-storage#endpoint-types) for more information.|
|» label|body|string|true|The name for this bucket.<br><br>* A bucket name can contain from 3 to 63 alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), or dots (`.`).<br>* A bucket name can't end in a dash and you can't use two consecutive dashes.<br>* A bucket name can't start or end in a dot, and you can't use two consecutive dots. As a best practice, only use dots if a certificate you're using with your bucket requires it. (For example, if you're using a custom TLS certificate.)<br>* A bucket name needs to be unique in the `region` where you're creating the bucket. The API only reserves labels for the `region` where active buckets are created and stored. If you want to reserve this bucket's label in another `region`, create a new bucket with the same label in the new `region`.|
|» region|body|string|false|The `id` assigned to the data center ([region](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-regions)) where this Object Storage bucket should be created.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> This supports legacy `clusterId` values that represented a specific region. For example, `us-east-1` is the legacy reference for the `us-east` region.|
|» s3_endpoint|body|string|false|The active user's S3-compatible endpoint URL, based on the `endpoint_type` and `region`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|
|» acl|private|
|» acl|public-read|
|» acl|authenticated-read|
|» acl|public-read-write|
|» endpoint_type|E0|
|» endpoint_type|E1|
|» endpoint_type|E2|
|» endpoint_type|E3|

  "label": "primary-bucket",

## Remove an Object Storage bucket

<a id="opIddelete-object-storage-bucket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets/%7B%7BregionId%7D%7D/%7B%7Bbucket%7D%7D \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets/{regionId}/{bucket}`

Removes a single bucket.

> 📘
>
> - You need to remove all objects from a bucket before you can delete it. While you can delete a bucket using the [CLI](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/storage/object-storage/guides/s3cmd/#delete-a-bucket), this operation fails if the bucket contains too many objects. The best way to empty large buckets is to configure lifecycle policies with an outside API, such as the [Ceph Object Gateway S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/bucketpolicy/#). Set a policy to remove all objects, wait a day or more for the system to remove all objects, then delete the bucket.
>
> - You can use an outside API, such as the [Ceph Object Gateway S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/bucketops/#delete-bucket) for more options.

## Update an object's ACL configuration

<a id="opIdput-object-storage-bucket-acl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets/%7B%7BregionId%7D%7D/%7B%7Bbucket%7D%7D/object-acl \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "acl": "{{acl}}",
    "name": "{{name}}"
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets/{regionId}/{bucket}/object-acl`

Update a specific object's access control list (ACL) settings. ACLs define who can access your buckets and objects, and specify the level of access granted to those users.

> 📘
>
> You can use an outside API, such as the [Ceph Object Gateway S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/objectops/#set-object-acl) for more options.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    object_storage:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-object-storage-bucket-acl">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acl": "{{acl}}",
  "name": "{{name}}"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|regionId|path|string|true|Identifies a region where this bucket lives.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> You can use a `clusterId` in place of `regionId` in requests for buckets that you created using the legacy version of the API. Run [List clusters](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-object-storage-clusters) to see each cluster `id`.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» acl|body|string|true|The S3 predefined collection of grantees and permissions set for the bucket, also referred to as a [Canned ACL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/acl-overview.html#canned-acl).|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the object where access control list (ACL) settings will be updated. Run the [List Object Storage bucket contents](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-object-storage-bucket-content) operation to access all object names in a bucket.|

## List Object Storage bucket contents

<a id="opIdget-object-storage-bucket-content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets/%7B%7BregionId%7D%7D/%7B%7Bbucket%7D%7D/object-list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets/{regionId}/{bucket}/object-list`

Returns the contents of a bucket. The contents are paginated using a `marker`, that's the name of the last object on the previous page. Objects can also be filtered by `prefix` and `delimiter`. See [Filtering and sorting](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/filtering-and-sorting) for more information.

> 📘
>
> You can use an outside API, such as the [Ceph Object Gateway S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/objectops/#get-object) for more options.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    object_storage:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-object-storage-bucket-content">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

<h3 id="list-object-storage-bucket-contents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|marker|query|string|false|The "marker" for this request, which can be used to paginate through large buckets. Its value should be the value of the `next_marker` property returned with the last page. Listing bucket contents _does not_ support arbitrary page access. See the `next_marker` property in the responses section for more details.|
|delimiter|query|string|false|The delimiter for object names; if given, object names will be returned up to the first occurrence of this character. This is most commonly used with the `/` character to allow bucket transversal in a manner similar to a filesystem, however any delimiter may be used. Use in conjunction with `prefix` to see object names past the first occurrence of the delimiter.|
|prefix|query|string|false|Filters objects returned to only those whose name start with the given prefix. Commonly used in conjunction with `delimiter` to allow transversal of bucket contents in a manner similar to a filesystem.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|regionId|path|string|true|Identifies a region where this bucket lives.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> You can use a `clusterId` in place of `regionId` in requests for buckets that you created using the legacy version of the API. Run [List clusters](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-object-storage-clusters) to see each cluster `id`.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "etag": "9f254c71e28e033bf9e0e5262e3e72ab",
      "last_modified": "2019-01-01T01:23:45",
      "name": "example",
      "owner": "bfc70ab2-e3d4-42a4-ad55-83921822270c",
      "size": 123
    }
  ],
  "is_truncated": true,
  "next_marker": "bd021c21-e734-4823-97a4-58b41c2cd4c8.892602.184"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|One page of the requested bucket's contents.|Inline|
|default|Default|See [Errors](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/errors) for the range of possible error response codes.|Inline|

<h3 id="list-object-storage-bucket-contents-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|false|none|none|
|» etag|string|false|none|An MD-5 hash of the object. `null` if this object represents a prefix.|
|» last_modified|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time this object was last modified. `null` if this object represents a prefix.|
|» name|string|false|none|The name of this object or prefix.|
|» owner|string|false|none|The owner of this object, as a UUID. `null` if this object represents a prefix.|
|» size|integer|false|none|The size of this object, in bytes. `null` if this object represents a prefix.|
|is_truncated|boolean|false|none|Designates if there is another page of bucket objects.|
|next_marker|string \| null|false|none|Returns the value you should pass to the `marker` query parameter to get the next page of objects. If there is no next page, `null` will be returned.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|» reason|string|false|none|What happened to cause this error. In most cases, this can be fixed immediately by changing the data you sent in the request, but in some cases you will be instructed to [Open a support ticket](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-ticket) or perform some other action before you can complete the request successfully.|

## Create a URL for an object

<a id="opIdpost-object-storage-object-url"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets/%7B%7BregionId%7D%7D/%7B%7Bbucket%7D%7D/object-url \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "content_type": "{{content_type}}",
    "expires_in": "{{expires_in}}",
    "method": "{{method}}",
    "name": "{{name}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets/{regionId}/{bucket}/object-url`

Creates a pre-signed URL to access a single object in a bucket. Use it to share, create, or delete objects by using the appropriate HTTP method in your request body's `method` parameter.

> 📘
>
> You can use an outside API, such as the [Ceph Object Gateway S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/) for more options.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    object_storage:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-object-url">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content_type": "{{content_type}}",
  "expires_in": "{{expires_in}}",
  "method": "{{method}}",
  "name": "{{name}}"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-url-for-an-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|regionId|path|string|true|Identifies a region where this bucket lives.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> You can use a `clusterId` in place of `regionId` in requests for buckets that you created using the legacy version of the API. Run [List clusters](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-object-storage-clusters) to see each cluster `id`.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|
|body|body|object|false|Information about the request to sign.|
|» content_type|body|string \| null|false|The expected `Content-type` header of the request this signed URL will be valid for.  If provided, the `Content-type` header _must_ be sent with the request when this URL is used, and _must_ be the same as it was when the signed URL was created. Required for all methods _except_ `GET` or `DELETE`.|
|» expires_in|body|integer \| null|false|How long this signed URL will be valid for, in seconds.  If omitted, the URL will be valid for 3600 seconds (1 hour).|
|» method|body|string|true|The HTTP method allowed to be used with the pre-signed URL.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the object that will be accessed with the pre-signed URL. This object need not exist, and no error will be returned if it doesn't. This behavior is useful for generating pre-signed URLs to upload new objects to by setting the `method` to `PUT`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "url": "https://us-east-1.linodeobjects.com/example-bucket/example?Signature=qr98TEucCntPgEG%2BsZQGDsJg93c%3D&Expires=1567609905&AWSAccessKeyId=G4YAF81XWY61DQM94SE0"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The URL with which to access your object.|Inline|
|default|Default|See [Errors](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/errors) for the range of possible error response codes.|Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-url-for-an-object-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|url|string|false|none|The signed URL to perform the request at.|

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» reason|string|false|none|What happened to cause this error. In most cases, this can be fixed immediately by changing the data you sent in the request, but in some cases you will be instructed to [Open a support ticket](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-ticket) or perform some other action before you can complete the request successfully.|

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-tlsssl-certificates">TLS/SSL certificates</h1>

You can set up TLS/SSL certificates to secure the connection to the domain you set up for your Object Storage buckets. Use these operations to add, view, and delete these certificates.

<a id="opIdget-object-storage-ssl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets/%7B%7BregionId%7D%7D/%7B%7Bbucket%7D%7D/ssl \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets/{regionId}/{bucket}/ssl`

Returns a boolean value indicating if this bucket has a corresponding TLS/SSL certificate that was uploaded by an Account user.

## Upload an Object Storage TLS/SSL certificate

<a id="opIdpost-object-storage-ssl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/buckets/%7B%7BregionId%7D%7D/%7B%7Bbucket%7D%7D/ssl \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "certificate": "{{certificate}}",
    "private_key": "{{private_key}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/object-storage/buckets/{regionId}/{bucket}/ssl`

Upload a TLS/SSL certificate and private key to be served when you visit your Object Storage bucket via HTTPS. Your TLS/SSL certificate and private key are stored encrypted at rest.

To replace an expired certificate, [delete your current certificates](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-object-storage-ssl) and upload a new one.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli object-storage ssl-upload \
  us-east-1 example-bucket \
  --certificate "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
                 CERTIFICATE_INFORMATION
                 -----END CERTIFICATE-----" \
  --private_key "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
                 PRIVATE_KEY_INFORMATION
                 -----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    object_storage:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|
|body|body|object|false|Upload this TLS/SSL certificate with its corresponding secret key.|
|» certificate|body|string|true|Your Base64 encoded and PEM formatted SSL certificate.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as `\n` in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI)|
|» private_key|body|string|true|The private key associated with this TLS/SSL certificate.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as `\n` in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI)|

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-endpoints">Endpoints</h1>

An endpoint is the S3-compatible URL to an Object Storage bucket. Use these operations to review details about your endpoints.

<a id="opIdget-object-storage-endpoints"></a>

`GET /{apiVersion}/object-storage/endpoints`

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-access-keys">Access keys</h1>

Object Storage keys are used to authenticate access to your Object Storage buckets. Use these operations to create, view, update, and revoke these keys.
