## Create an Object Storage access key

<a id="opIdpost-object-storage-keys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bucket_access": [
      {
        "bucket_name": "primary-bucket",
        "permissions": "read_only",
        "region": "us-iad"
      }
    ],
    "label": "my-key"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/object-storage/keys`

Generates a new Object Storage access key and an associated secret key. The secret key is only displayed when the access key is generated and cannot be viewed again. A successful request triggers an `obj_access_key_create` [event](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-events).

> 📘
>
> - Accounts with negative balances can't access this operation.
>
> - This operation has specific [rate limits](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/rate-limits#specific-operation-rate-limits).

**Unlimited vs. limited access keys**

An unlimited access key grants full access to all of your buckets in each region you name, using the `regions` array. A limited access key lets you name specific buckets where you need to manage content, using the `bucket_access` array.

> 👍 There's a tutorial
>
> We offer workflows for both an [unlimited access key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/create-an-unlimited-access-key) and a [limited access key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/create-a-limited-access-key).


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli object-storage keys-create \
  --label "my-object-storage-key" \
  --bucket_access '[{"region": "ap-south", "bucket_name": "bucket-example-1", "permissions": "read_write" }]'
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    object_storage:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-keys">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json

  "bucket_access": [
    {
      "bucket_name": "primary-bucket",
      "permissions": "read_only",
      "region": "us-iad"
    }
  ],
  "label": "my-key"
}
```

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|bucket_access|[object]|false|none|Settings that limit access to specific buckets, each with a specific permission level. See [Create a limited access key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-keys) for more information.|

|» cluster|string|false|none|__Deprecated__ For backwards compatibility, this is included to identify the legacy cluster equivalent of the `region` where this key can be used. The key grants access to each specified `bucket_name`, based on the `permissions` set.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> Use of clusters in a limited access key has been deprecated.|
|» permissions|string|false|none|The level of access the key grants to the `bucket_name`. Keys with `read_write` access can manage content in the `bucket_name`, while `read_only` can be used to view content.|
|» region|string|false|none|The region where the `bucket_name` resides.|
|id|integer|false|none|This Object Storage key's unique ID.|
|label|string|false|none|The label given to this key. For display purposes only.|
|limited|boolean|false|none|Whether this Object Storage key limits access to specific buckets and permissions. Returns `false` if this key grants full access. Specific limitations are set in `bucket_access`.|
|regions|[object]|false|none|The key can be used in these regions to manage buckets.|
|» endpoint_type|string|false|none|The type of `s3_endpoint` available to the active `user` in this `region`. See [Endpoint types](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/object-storage#endpoint-types) for more information.|
|» id|string|false|none|Identifies each region where you can use the Object Storage key.<br><br>- **For an unlimited key**. See [Create an unlimited access key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-keys) for more information.<br><br>- **For a limited access key**. The API server populates each object in this array with each of the individual instances of the `region` parameter you set in the `bucket_access` array. See [Create a limited access key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-keys) for more information.|
|» s3_endpoint|string|false|none|The S3-compatible hostname you can use to access the Object Storage buckets in this region.|
|secret_key|string|false|none|This Object Storage key's secret key. Used as a password to validate this key when making requests to an S3 API, such as the Amazon S3 API or Ceph Object Gateway S3 API.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> This value is listed as `[REDACTED]` for this operation, to protect it. It's only revealed in a response after [creating](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-keys) a key.|

## Update an Object Storage access key

<a id="opIdput-object-storage-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/keys/%7B%7BkeyId%7D%7D \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "access_key": "ABCDEFGHI1JKL2MNOP34",
    "id": 123,
    "label": "my-key",
    "limited": true,
    "regions": [
      {
        "endpoint_type": "E1",
        "id": "us-west",
        "s3_endpoint": "us-west-00.linodeobjects.com"
      }
    ],
    "secret_key": "[REDACTED]"
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/object-storage/keys/{keyId}`

Updates an Object Storage access key on your account. A successful request triggers an `obj_access_key_update` [event](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-events).

> 📘
>
> This operation has specific [rate limits](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/rate-limits#specific-operation-rate-limits).


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli object-storage keys-update \
  --keyId 12345
  --label "my-object-storage-key"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    object_storage:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-object-storage-key">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_key": "ABCDEFGHI1JKL2MNOP34",
  "id": 123,
  "label": "my-key",
  "limited": true,
  "regions": [
    {
      "endpoint_type": "E1",
      "id": "us-west",
      "s3_endpoint": "us-west-00.linodeobjects.com"
    }
  ],
  "secret_key": "[REDACTED]"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-object-storage-access-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|keyId|path|integer|true|The key to look up.|
|body|body|object|false|The fields to update.|
|» label|body|string|false|The label for the Object Storage key. Used for display purposes. Omit this to leave the `label` unchanged.|
|» regions|body|[string]|false|Replace the current list of `regions` set in a specific key. Include an existing region to keep it, or leave it out to remove it. Omit the `regions` array to leave the existing list unchanged. If you include new `regions` in the key, you can't immediately use the key to manage content in buckets in those regions. You need to grant these keys this access using [bucket policies](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/storage/object-storage/guides/bucket-policies/).<br><br>> 🚧 Limited keys have restrictions<br>><br>> These points apply to keys you've [created](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-object-storage-keys) using the `bucket_access` array:<br>><br>> - You can't remove a `region` from a limited key's original `bucket_access` list. If you include the `regions` array in this operation and target a limited key, you need to include all existing `region` entries from the `bucket_access` array. Otherwise, the operation fails with an error. Run [Get an Object Storage key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-object-storage-key) to review current `region` entries in a limited key.<br>><br>> - If you need to remove a specific region from an active limited key, you can [revoke the key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-object-storage-key) and create a new Object Storage key, without the specific region.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|

```json
  "limited": true,
  "regions": [
    {
      "endpoint_type": "E1",
      "id": "us-west",
      "s3_endpoint": "us-west-00.linodeobjects.com"
    }
  ],

}
```

```json
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Revoke an Object Storage access key

<a id="opIddelete-object-storage-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/object-storage/keys/%7B%7BkeyId%7D%7D \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/object-storage/keys/{keyId}`

Revokes an Object Storage access key. Once revoked, the access key can no longer be used by third-party clients. A successful request triggers an `obj_access_key_delete` [event](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-events).

> 📘
>
> This operation has specific [rate limits](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/rate-limits#specific-operation-rate-limits).

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-trusted-devices">Trusted devices</h1>

View details about trusted devices associated with your user account. If needed, you can revoke a trusted device so any future login attempts from that device will go through the full authentication process.

## List trusted devices

<a id="opIdget-devices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/devices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/profile/devices`

Returns a paginated list of active trusted devices for your user. Browsers with an active Remember Me Session are logged into your account until the session expires or is revoked.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli profile devices-list
    ```

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-grants">Grants</h1>

View the grants (permissions) available to your user account.

## List grants

<a id="opIdget-profile-grants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/grants \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/profile/grants`

This returns a GrantsResponse describing what the acting User has been granted access to.  For unrestricted users, this will return a  204 and no body because unrestricted users have access to everything without grants.  This will not return information about entities you do not have access to.  This operation is useful when writing third-party OAuth applications to see what options you should present to the acting User.

For example, if they do not have `global.add_linodes`, you might not display a button to deploy a new Linode.

Any client may run this operation; no OAuth scopes are required.

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-profile-grants">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-phone-number">Phone number</h1>

Operations to verify and delete the phone number associated with your user account, which is used to send SMS messages as a form of two-factor authentication (2FA).

## Send a phone number verification code

<a id="opIdpost-profile-phone-number"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/phone-number \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "iso_code": "{{iso_code}}",
    "phone_number": "{{phone_number}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/profile/phone-number`

Send a one-time verification code via SMS message to the submitted phone number. Providing your phone number helps ensure you can securely access your Account in case other ways to connect are lost. Your phone number is only used to verify your identity by sending an SMS message. Standard carrier messaging fees may apply.

- By accessing this operation you are opting in to receive SMS messages. You can opt out of SMS messages by running the [Delete a phone number](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-profile-phone-number) operation after your phone number is verified.

- Verification codes are valid for 10 minutes after they are sent.

- Subsequent requests made prior to code expiration result in sending the same code.

Once a verification code is received, verify your phone number with the [Verify a phone number](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-profile-phone-number-verify) operation.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli phone sms-code-send \
  --iso-code US \
  --phone-number 555-555-5555
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-profile-phone-number">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

```json
}
```

## Verify a phone number

<a id="opIdpost-profile-phone-number-verify"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/phone-number/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "otp_code": "{{otp_code}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/profile/phone-number/verify`

Verify a phone number by confirming the one-time code received via SMS message after running the [Send a phone number verification code](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-profile-phone-number) operation.

- Verification codes are valid for 10 minutes after they are sent.

- Only the same User that made the verification code request can use that code with this operation.

Once completed, the verified phone number is assigned to the User making the request. To change the verified phone number for a User, first run the [Delete a phone number](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-profile-phone-number) operation, then begin the verification process again with the [Send a phone number verification code](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-profile-phone-number) operation.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli phone verify \
  --otp_code 123456
    ```

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-oauth-preferences">OAuth preferences</h1>

## Get user preferences

<a id="opIdget-user-preferences"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/preferences \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/profile/preferences`

View a list of user preferences tied to the OAuth client that generated the token making the request. The user preferences endpoints allow consumers of the API to store arbitrary JSON data, such as a user's font size preference or preferred display name. User preferences are available for each OAuth client registered to your account, and as such an account can have multiple user preferences.

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/security-questions \
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/profile/security-questions`

Adds security question responses for your user. You need to use exactly three unique questions. Previous responses are overwritten if answered, or they're reset to `null` if unanswered.

> 📘

> You need to answer these security questions before you can access the [Create a two factor secret](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-tfa-enable) operation.

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-ssh-keys">SSH keys</h1>

Manage SSH keys for your user account. When creating a Linode, you can choose to have one or more SSH keys automatically added to the new Linode for secure access.

## List SSH keys

<a id="opIdget-ssh-keys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/sshkeys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/profile/sshkeys`

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-two-factor-authentication">Two-factor authentication</h1>

Enable or disable two-factor authentication (2FA) on your user account to prevent unauthorized logins.

## Disable two-factor authentication

<a id="opIdpost-tfa-disable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/tfa-disable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/profile/tfa-disable`

Disables two-factor authentication (2FA) for your user. Once successful, login attempts from untrusted computers will only require a password. Keep 2FA enabled to protect your account.


<<LB>>

---

    ```
    linode-cli profile tfa-disable
    ```

## Generate a secret key for two-factor authentication

<a id="opIdpost-tfa-enable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/tfa-enable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/profile/tfa-enable`

Generates a secret key for your user. To enable two-factor authentication (2FA), enter this secret into your third-party authenticator application. To complete the 2FA setup, use the [Enable two-factor authentication](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-tfa-confirm) operation to enter a one-time passcode (OTP) from your authenticator app. Once enabled, logins from untrusted computers are required to provide an OTP before they are successful.

Run the [Answer security questions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-security-questions) operation.

---

    ```
    linode-cli profile tfa-enable
    ```

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

## Enable two-factor authentication

<a id="opIdpost-tfa-confirm"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/tfa-enable-confirm \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tfa_code": "{{tfa_code}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/profile/tfa-enable-confirm`

Confirms that you can successfully generate one-time codes. Once confirmed, 2FA is enabled on your account. Login attempts from untrusted computers will be required to provide a one-time code before they are successful.

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-personal-access-tokens">Personal access tokens</h1>

Manage personal access tokens for your user account. Personal access tokens can be used for authentication with the Linode API.

## List personal access tokens

<a id="opIdget-personal-access-tokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/profile/tokens`

Returns a paginated list of Personal Access Tokens currently active for your User.

## Create a personal access token

<a id="opIdpost-personal-access-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expiry": "{{expiry}}",
    "label": "{{label}}",
    "scopes": "{{scopes}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/profile/tokens`

Creates a Personal Access Token for your User. The raw token will be returned in the response, but will never be returned again afterward so be sure to take note of it. You may create a token with _at most_ the scopes of your current token. The created token will be able to access your Account until the given expiry, or until it is revoked. __Parent and child accounts__ In a [parent and child account](https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/parent-child-accounts/) environment, the following apply:

- If you're using a child account parent user (proxy user), you can't create this form of token. The only token available to a proxy user is one that lets you run operations in a child account. These are created with the [Create a proxy user token](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-child-account-token) operation.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli profile token-create \
  --scopes '*' \
  --expiry '2018-01-01T13:46:32' \
  --label linode-cli
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-personal-access-token">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiry": "{{expiry}}",
  "label": "{{label}}",
  "scopes": "{{scopes}}"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-personal-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the requested token.|
|» expiry|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|When this token should be valid until.  If omitted, the new token will be valid until it is manually revoked.|
|» label|body|string|false|__Filterable__ This token's label.  This is for display purposes only, but can be used to more easily track what you're using each token for.|
|» scopes|body|string(oauth-scope)|false|The access [scopes](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth-reference) to grant to the created token. These cannot be changed after creation, and may not exceed the scopes of the acting token.<br><br>If omitted or entered with a wildcard character (`*`), the new token will have the same scopes as the acting token.<br><br>Multiple scopes are separated by a space character (` `).<br><br>For example, `linodes:read_write account:read_only`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|

```json
  "expiry": "2018-01-01T13:46:32",
  "id": 123,

  "scopes": "*",
  "token": "abcdefghijklmnop"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

Tokens may be created with `null` as their expiry and will never expire unless revoked.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ This token's unique ID, which can be used to revoke it.|
|label|string|false|none|__Filterable__ This token's label.  This is for display purposes only, but can be used to more easily track what you're using each token for.|
|scopes|string(oauth-scopes)|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The scopes this token was created with. These define what parts of the Account the token can be used to access. Many command-line tools, such as the [Linode CLI](https://github.com/linode/linode-cli), require tokens with access to `*`. Tokens with more restrictive scopes are generally more secure.|
|token|string|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The token used to access the API.  When the token is created, the full token is returned here.  Otherwise, only the first 16 characters are returned.|

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|false|none|none|
|» field|string|false|none|The field in the request that caused this error. This may be a path, separated by periods in the case of nested fields. In some cases this may come back as `null` if the error is not specific to any single element of the request.|
|» reason|string|false|none|What happened to cause this error. In most cases, this can be fixed immediately by changing the data you sent in the request, but in some cases you will be instructed to [Open a support ticket](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-ticket) or perform some other action before you can complete the request successfully.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: account:read_write )
</aside>

## Revoke a personal access token

<a id="opIddelete-personal-access-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/profile/tokens/%7B%7BtokenId%7D%7D \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/profile/tokens/{tokenId}`

Revokes a Personal Access Token. The token will be invalidated immediately, and requests using that token will fail with a 401. It is possible to revoke access to the token making the request to revoke a token, but keep in mind that doing so could lose you access to the api and require you to create a new token through some other means.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli profile token-delete 123
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-personal-access-token">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-support-tickets">Support tickets</h1>

Use these operations to open, view, and close support tickets, when you need assistance from Akamai.

## List support tickets

<a id="opIdget-tickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/support/tickets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/support/tickets`

Returns a collection of all support tickets opened from your account. This includes tickets you've opened and tickets generated by Linode customer support regarding your account. Open tickets are returned first in the response.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli tickets list
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-tickets">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

## Open a support ticket

<a id="opIdpost-ticket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/support/tickets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bucket": "{{bucket}}",
    "database_id": "{{database_id}}",
    "description": "{{description}}",
    "domain_id": "{{domain_id}}",
    "firewall_id": "{{firewall_id}}",
    "linode_id": "{{linode_id}}",
    "lkecluster_id": "{{lkecluster_id}}",
    "longviewclient_id": "{{longviewclient_id}}",
    "managed_issue": "{{managed_issue}}",
    "nodebalancer_id": "{{nodebalancer_id}}",
    "region": "{{region}}",
    "severity": "{{severity}}",
    "summary": "{{summary}}",
    "vlan": "{{vlan}}",
    "volume_id": "{{volume_id}}",
    "vpc_id": "{{vpc_id}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/support/tickets`

Open a support ticket. A ticket can only target a single, specific entity. For example, for an issue with a specific Linode, open a ticket and target it using its `linode_id`. Leave all other entities out of the request or set them to `null`.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli tickets create \
  --description "I'm having trouble setting the root password on my Linode. I tried following the instructions but something is not working and I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong. Can you please help me figure out how I can reset it?" \
  --linode_id 123 \
  --summary "Having trouble resetting root password on my Linode"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-ticket">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bucket": "{{bucket}}",
  "database_id": "{{database_id}}",
  "description": "{{description}}",
  "domain_id": "{{domain_id}}",
  "firewall_id": "{{firewall_id}}",
  "linode_id": "{{linode_id}}",
  "lkecluster_id": "{{lkecluster_id}}",
  "longviewclient_id": "{{longviewclient_id}}",
  "managed_issue": "{{managed_issue}}",
  "nodebalancer_id": "{{nodebalancer_id}}",
  "region": "{{region}}",
  "severity": "{{severity}}",
  "summary": "{{summary}}",
  "vlan": "{{vlan}}",
  "volume_id": "{{volume_id}}",
  "vpc_id": "{{vpc_id}}"
}
```

<h3 id="open-a-support-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» bucket|body|string \| null|false|The name of an Object Storage bucket entity for this ticket. Run the [List Object Storage buckets](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-object-storage-buckets) operation and store the `label` for the target bucket. You also need to provide the specific `region` where the bucket is located.|
|» database_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the Managed Database entity for the ticket. Run the [List Managed Databases](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-databases-instances) operation and store the `id` for the target database.|
|» description|body|string|true|The full details of the issue or question.|
|» domain_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the domain entity for the ticket. Run the [List domains](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-domains) operation and store the `id` for the target domain.|
|» firewall_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the Firewall entity for the ticket. Run the [List a Linode's firewalls](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-linode-firewalls) operation and store the `id` for the target Linode firewall.|
|» linode_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the Linode entity for the ticket. Run the [List Linodes](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-linode-instances) operation and store the `id` for the target Linode.|
|» lkecluster_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE) cluster entity for the ticket. Run the [List Kubernetes clusters](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-lke-clusters) operation and store the `id` for the target LKE cluster.|
|» longviewclient_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the Longview client entity for the ticket. Run the [List Longview clients](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-longview-clients) operation and store the `id` for the target client.|
|» managed_issue|body|boolean|false|Whether this ticket is related to a [managed service](https://www.linode.com/products/managed/). If `true`, the following constraints apply:<br><br>- You can't provide an entity, such as a `linode_id` or `bucket` with this request.<br><br>- Your account needs a managed service [enabled](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-enable-managed-service).|
|» nodebalancer_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the NodeBalancer entity for the ticket. Run the [List NodeBalancers](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-node-balancers) operation and store the `id` for the target NodeBalancer.|
|» region|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the [region](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-regions) where this ticket's target entity resides. This only applies to tickets for a `vlan` or an Object Storage  `bucket`.<br><br>> 📘<br>><br>> Set this to the `clusterId` for a legacy Object Storage `bucket`.|
|» severity|body|integer \| null|false|The severity of the issue. A value of `1` indicates a major issue, `2` indicates a moderate priority issue, and `3` is a low priority issue. Your account may not have access to set this value. Talk to your Akamai account team for more details.|
|» summary|body|string|true|The summary or title for this support ticket.|
|» vlan|body|string \| null|false|The label of the VLAN entity for the ticket. Run the [List VLANs](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-vlans) operation and store the `id` for the target VLAN. You also need to provide the specific `region` where the VLAN is located.|
|» volume_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the volume entity for the ticket. Run the [List volumes](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-volumes) operation and store the `id` for the target volume.|
|» vpc_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the VPC entity for the ticket. Run the [List VPCs](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-vpcs) operation and store the `id` for the target VPC.|

|apiVersion|v4beta|

|» severity|3|

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-attachments">Attachments</h1>

Mange any attachments you may need to include with your support tickets, such as log entry files and screenshot images.

## Create a support ticket attachment

<a id="opIdpost-ticket-attachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/support/tickets/%7B%7BticketId%7D%7D/attachments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=/Users/LinodeGuy/pictures/screen_shot.jpg'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/support/tickets/{ticketId}/attachments`

Adds a file attachment to an open support ticket on your account. Use an attachment to help customer support resolve your ticket. The file attachment is submitted in the request as `multipart/form-data` type. Accepted file extensions include: `.gif`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.pjpg`, `.pjpeg`, `.tif`, `.tiff`, `.png`, `.pdf`, or `.txt`.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)


`GET /{apiVersion}/account/oauth-clients/{clientId}/thumbnail`

Returns the PNG thumbnail for this OAuth client.  This is a publicly viewable operation, and you can access it without authentication.

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-client-thumbnail">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|clientId|path|string|true|The OAuth Client ID to look up.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» reason|string|false|none|What happened to cause this error. In most cases, this can be fixed immediately by changing the data you sent in the request, but in some cases you will be instructed to [Open a support ticket](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-ticket) or perform some other action before you can complete the request successfully.|

## Update the OAuth client's thumbnail

<a id="opIdput-client-thumbnail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/account/oauth-clients/%7B%7BclientId%7D%7D/thumbnail \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: image/png' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/account/oauth-clients/{clientId}/thumbnail`

Upload a thumbnail for a client you own. You need to upload a PNG image file that the Linode API returns when the thumbnail is retrieved. This image is publicly viewable.


<<LB>>

---


- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

|body|body|string(binary)|true|The image to set as the thumbnail.|

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-records">Records</h1>

## List domain records

<a id="opIdget-domain-records"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/domains/%7B%7BdomainId%7D%7D/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/domains/{domainId}/records`

Returns a paginated list of Records configured on a Domain in Linode's DNS Manager.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli domains records-list 1234
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    domains:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-domain-records">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

<h3 id="list-domain-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of a collection to return.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|apiVersion|path|string|true|__Enum__ Call either the `v4` URL, or `v4beta` for operations still in Beta.|
|domainId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Domain we are accessing Records for.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|v4|
|apiVersion|v4beta|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
      "id": 123456,
      "name": "test",
      "port": 80,
      "priority": 50,
      "protocol": null,
      "service": null,
      "tag": null,
      "target": "192.0.2.0",
      "ttl_sec": 604800,
      "type": "A",
      "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
      "weight": 50
    }
  ],
  "page": 1,
  "pages": 1,
  "results": 1
}
```

<h3 id="list-domain-records-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A list of Domain Records.|Inline|

<h3 id="list-domain-records-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|false|none|none|
|» created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|__Read-only__ When this Domain Record was created.|
|» id|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ This Record's unique ID.|
|» name|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The name of this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The hostname or FQDN of the Record.<br><br>`NS`: The subdomain, if any, to use with the Domain of the Record. Wildcard NS records (`*`) are not supported.<br><br>`MX`: The mail subdomain. For example, `sub` for the address `user@sub.example.com` under the `example.com` Domain.<br><br>- The left-most subdomain component may be an asterisk (`*`) to designate a wildcard subdomain.<br>- Other subdomain components must only contain letters, digits, and hyphens, start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain less than 64 characters.<br>- Must be an empty string (`""`) for a Null MX Record.<br><br>`CNAME`: The hostname. Must be unique. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The hostname.<br><br>`SRV`: Unused. Use the `service` property to set the service name for this record.<br><br>`CAA`: The subdomain. Omit or enter an empty string (`""`) to apply to the entire Domain.<br><br>`PTR`: See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).|
|» port|integer|false|none|The port this Record points to. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.|
|» priority|integer|false|none|The priority of the target host for this Record. Lower values are preferred. Only valid for MX and SRV record requests. Required for SRV record requests.<br><br>Defaults to `0` for MX record requests. Must be `0` for Null MX records.|
|» protocol|string \| null|false|none|The protocol this Record's service communicates with. An underscore (`_`) is prepended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid for SRV record requests.|
|» service|string \| null|false|none|The name of the service. An underscore (`_`) is prepended and a period (`.`) is appended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.|
|» tag|string \| null|false|none|__Filterable__ The tag portion of a CAA record. Only valid and required for CAA record requests.|
|» target|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The target for this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The IP address. Use `[remote_addr]` to submit the IPv4 address of the request. Required.<br><br>`NS`: The name server. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`MX`: The mail server. Must be a valid domain unless creating a Null MX Record. Required.<br><br>- Must have less than 254 total characters.<br>- The left-most domain component may be an asterisk (`*`) to designate a wildcard domain.<br>- Other domain components must only contain letters, digits, and hyphens, start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain less than 64 characters.<br>- To create a [Null MX Record](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7505), first [remove](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-domain-record) any additional MX records, then create an MX record with empty strings (`""`) for the `target` and `name`. If a Domain has a Null MX record, new MX records cannot be created.<br><br>`CNAME`: The alias. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The value. Required.<br><br>`SRV`: The target domain or subdomain. If a subdomain is entered, it is automatically used with the Domain.<br>To configure for a different domain, enter a valid FQDN. For example, the value `www` with a Domain for<br>`example.com` results in a target set to `www.example.com`, whereas the value `sample.com` results in a<br>target set to `sample.com`. Required.<br><br>`CAA`: The value. For `issue` or `issuewild` tags, the domain of your certificate issuer. For the `iodef`<br>tag, a contact or submission URL (domain, http, https, or mailto). Requirements depend on the tag for this record:<br><br>  - `issue`: The domain of your certificate issuer. Must include a valid domain. May include additional parameters separated with semicolons (`;`), for example: `www.example.com; foo=bar`<br>  - `issuewild`: The domain of your wildcard certificate issuer. Must be a valid domain and must not start with an asterisk (`*`).<br>  - `iodef`: Must be either (1) a valid domain, (2) a valid domain prepended with `http://` or `https://`, or (3) a valid email address prepended with `mailto:`.<br><br>`PTR`: Required. See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br><br>With the exception of A, AAAA, and CAA records, this field accepts a trailing period.|
|» ttl_sec|integer|false|none|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers. Valid values are 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200 - any other value will be rounded to the nearest valid value.|
|» type|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The type of Record this is in the DNS system. For example, A records associate a domain name with an IPv4 address, and AAAA records associate a domain name with an IPv6 address. For more information, see the guides on [DNS Record Types](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/networking/dns-manager/guides/#dns-record-types).|
|» updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|__Read-only__ When this Domain Record was last updated.|
|» weight|integer|false|none|The relative weight of this Record used in the case of identical priority. Higher values are preferred. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.|
|page|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The current [page](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/pagination).|
|pages|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The total number of [pages](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/pagination).|
|results|integer|false|read-only|__Read-only__ The total number of results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» tag|issue|
|» tag|issuewild|
|» tag|iodef|
|» type|A|
|» type|AAAA|
|» type|NS|
|» type|MX|
|» type|CNAME|
|» type|TXT|
|» type|SRV|
|» type|PTR|
|» type|CAA|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: domains:read_only )
</aside>

## Create a domain record

<a id="opIdpost-domain-record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/domains/%7B%7BdomainId%7D%7D/records \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "test",
    "port": 80,
    "priority": 50,
    "protocol": null,
    "service": null,
    "tag": null,
    "target": "192.0.2.0",
    "ttl_sec": 604800,
    "type": "A",
    "weight": 50
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/domains/{domainId}/records`

Adds a new Domain Record to the zonefile this Domain represents.

Each domain can have up to 12,000 active records.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli domains records-create 123 \
  --type A \
  --name test \
  --target 203.0.113.1 \
  --priority 50 \
  --weight 50 \
  --port 80 \
  --ttl_sec 604800
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    domains:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-domain-record">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "test",
  "port": 80,
  "priority": 50,
  "protocol": null,
  "service": null,
  "tag": null,
  "target": "192.0.2.0",
  "ttl_sec": 604800,
  "type": "A",
  "weight": 50
}
```

Required.<br><br>- Must have less than 254 total characters.<br>- The left-most domain component may be an asterisk (`*`) to designate a wildcard domain.<br>- Other domain components must only contain letters, digits, and hyphens, start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain less than 64 characters.<br>- To create a [Null MX Record](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7505), first [remove](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-domain-record) any additional MX records, then create an MX record with empty strings (`""`) for the `target` and `name`. If a Domain has a Null MX record, new MX records cannot be created.<br><br>`CNAME`: The alias. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The value. Required.<br><br>`SRV`: The target domain or subdomain. If a subdomain is entered, it is automatically used with the Domain.<br>To configure for a different domain, enter a valid FQDN. For example, the value `www` with a Domain for<br>`example.com` results in a target set to `www.example.com`, whereas the value `sample.com` results in a<br>target set to `sample.com`. Required.<br><br>`CAA`: The value. For `issue` or `issuewild` tags, the domain of your certificate issuer. For the `iodef`<br>tag, a contact or submission URL (domain, http, https, or mailto). Requirements depend on the tag for this record:<br><br>  - `issue`: The domain of your certificate issuer. Must include a valid domain. May include additional parameters separated with semicolons (`;`), for example: `www.example.com; foo=bar`<br>  - `issuewild`: The domain of your wildcard certificate issuer. Must be a valid domain and must not start with an asterisk (`*`).<br>  - `iodef`: Must be either (1) a valid domain, (2) a valid domain prepended with `http://` or `https://`, or (3) a valid email address prepended with `mailto:`.<br><br>`PTR`: Required. See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br><br>With the exception of A, AAAA, and CAA records, this field accepts a trailing period.|
|ttl_sec|integer|false|none|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers. Valid values are 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200 - any other value will be rounded to the nearest valid value.|
|type|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The type of Record this is in the DNS system. For example, A records associate a domain name with an IPv4 address, and AAAA records associate a domain name with an IPv6 address. For more information, see the guides on [DNS Record Types](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/networking/dns-manager/guides/#dns-record-types).|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|__Read-only__ When this Domain Record was last updated.|
|weight|integer|false|none|The relative weight of this Record used in the case of identical priority. Higher values are preferred. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.|

## Update a domain record

<a id="opIdput-domain-record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/domains/%7B%7BdomainId%7D%7D/records/%7B%7BrecordId%7D%7D \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "{{name}}",
    "port": "{{port}}",
    "priority": "{{priority}}",
    "protocol": "{{protocol}}",
    "service": "{{service}}",
    "tag": "{{tag}}",
    "target": "{{target}}",
    "ttl_sec": "{{ttl_sec}}",
    "weight": "{{weight}}"
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/domains/{domainId}/records/{recordId}`

Updates a single Record on this Domain.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli domains records-update 123 234 \
  --name test \
  --target 203.0.113.1 \
  --priority 50 \
  --weight 50 \
  --port 80 \
  --ttl_sec 604800
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br><br>With the exception of A, AAAA, and CAA records, this field accepts a trailing period.|
|ttl_sec|integer|false|none|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers. Valid values are 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200 - any other value will be rounded to the nearest valid value.|
|type|string|false|none|__Filterable__ The type of Record this is in the DNS system. For example, A records associate a domain name with an IPv4 address, and AAAA records associate a domain name with an IPv6 address. For more information, see the guides on [DNS Record Types](https://www.linode.com/docs/products/networking/dns-manager/guides/#dns-record-types).|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|__Read-only__ When this Domain Record was last updated.|
|weight|integer|false|none|The relative weight of this Record used in the case of identical priority. Higher values are preferred. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|tag|issue|
|tag|issuewild|
|tag|iodef|
|type|A|
|type|AAAA|
|type|NS|
|type|MX|
|type|CNAME|
|type|TXT|
|type|SRV|
|type|PTR|
|type|CAA|

## Create a share group

<a id="opIdpost-sharegroups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "{{description}}",
    "images": [
      {
        "description": "Official Debian Linux image for server deployment",
        "id": "private/7",
        "label": "Linux Debian"
      }
    ],
    "label": "{{label}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups`

Creates a group to share images with other users. 

- Include existing `images` in the request or [Add images to a share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-images) later. Run the [Get an image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-image) operation to see the existing images' `id` values. If needed, [Create an image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-image) or [Upload an image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-upload-image).

- You can set a `label` and `description` for the group and each image, visible to all group members. 

- If omitted, the shared image keeps the original `label` and `description`. Note that when you [Update the original image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-image), it has no effect on shared image's details within any groups.

- Run the [Add members to a share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-members) to include other users in the group. Use the group's `uuid` from the response to [Create a token](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-tokens) for user authentication.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups create --label "my_label" --description "my_description" \
  --images '[{"id": "private/15", "label": "Linux Debian", "description": "Official Debian Linux image for server deployment"}]'
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    images:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroups">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "{{description}}",
  "images": [
    {
      "description": "Official Debian Linux image for server deployment",
      "id": "private/7",
      "label": "Linux Debian"
    }
  ],
  "label": "{{label}}"
}
```

## Create a token

<a id="opIdpost-sharegroup-tokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "{{label}}",
    "valid_for_sharegroup_uuid": "{{valid_for_sharegroup_uuid}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/tokens`

Creates a single-use membership token for users who want to join a share group with custom images.

- Before creating a token, get the share group's UUID from its owner. The owner can run [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) or [Get a share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup) to get the group's UUID. If needed, [Create a share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroups) and share the UUID with the user.

- Share the `token` from the response with the share group owner. The owner can later use the token to [Add members to a share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-members) and manage the users' membership within the group.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups token-create --label "my_token" --valid_for_sharegroup_uuid "abc123"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    images:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-tokens">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "{{label}}",
  "valid_for_sharegroup_uuid": "{{valid_for_sharegroup_uuid}}"
}
```

## Get a share group

<a id="opIdget-sharegroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}`

Get information about an owned share group. Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group.

- If the `sharegroupId` in the request body belongs to a group you don't own, calling this API will result in a 404 error.

## Update a share group

<a id="opIdput-sharegroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "{{description}}",
    "label": "{{label}}"
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}`

Updates the details of a share group you own. Run this operation to edit the `label` or `description` of a particular sharegroup.

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group.

- You can update either of the fields, but when you provide a new `label`, make sure that it's not an empty string.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups update 1234 --label "new_label" --description "A new description."
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

## Add images to a share group

<a id="opIdpost-sharegroup-images"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D/images \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "images": [
      {
        "description": "Official Debian Linux image for server deployment",
        "id": "private/15",
        "label": "Linux Debian"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}/images`

Adds images to an existing group where you can share them with other members.

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group.

- Run the [Get an image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-image) operation to see the existing images' `id` values. If needed, [Create an image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-image) or [Upload an image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-upload-image).

- You can set a `label` and `description` for each image, visible to all group members. If omitted, the shared image keeps the original image's details. Note that when you [Update the original image](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-image), it has no effect on a shared image's details within any groups.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups image-add 123 \
  --images '[{"id": "private/15", "label": "Linux Debian", "description": "Official Debian Linux image for server deployment"}]'
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    images:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-images">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

```json
  ]
}
```

## Update a shared image

<a id="opIdput-sharegroup-imageshare"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D/images/%7B%7BimageId%7D%7D \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "{{description}}",
    "label": "{{label}}"
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}/images/{imageId}`

Updates the details of an image shared within a share group. Run this operation to edit the `label` and `description` of a particular shared image.

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group. To get the `imageID`, run the [List shared images by group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup-images) operation.

- You can update either of the fields, but when you provide a new `label`, make sure that it's not an empty string.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups image-update 123 1234 --label "new_label" --description "A new description."
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    images:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-sharegroup-imageshare">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

```json
  "label": "{{label}}"
}
```

## Revoke access to a shared image

<a id="opIddelete-sharegroup-imageshare"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D/images/%7B%7BimageId%7D%7D \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}/images/{imageId}`

Revokes access to a shared image within an owned group for all members.

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group. To get the `imageID`, run the [List shared images by group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup-images) operation.

- To add a private image back to a share group, run the [Add images to a share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-images).


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups image-remove 123 1234
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    images:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-sharegroup-imageshare">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

## Add members to a share group

<a id="opIdpost-sharegroup-members"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D/members \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "{{label}}",
    "token": "{{token}}"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}/members`

Adds users to existing shared private image groups as a group owner.

- Adding new members to share groups requires a single-use token. The user who wants to join a share group should run [Create a token](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-sharegroup-tokens) and share the `token` from the response with the group owner.

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups member-add 123 --token "abc123" --label "my_sharegroup_member"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    images:read_write
    ```

## Get a membership token

<a id="opIdget-sharegroup-member-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D/members/%7B%7BtokenUuid%7D%7D \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}/members/{tokenUuid}`

Get details about a membership token as a share group owner. Run this operation to check the `status` of a pending membership request or a current group member.

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group.

- Get the `token_uuid` from the user who wants to join your share group or run the [List members by share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup-members) operation for details on current group members.

- To get details about a token as a current or pending group member, run the [Get a token](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup-token) operation.


<<LB>>

---

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups member-view 123 abc123
    ```

## Update a membership token

<a id="opIdput-sharegroup-member-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D/members/%7B%7BtokenUuid%7D%7D \

    "label": "{{label}}"
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}/members/{tokenUuid}`

Updates an existing membership token for a group owner. You can change each token's `label` that will be visible only to you, such as when you [Get members by share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup-members).

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group.

- Run the [List members by share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup-members) operation to get the `token_uuid` for a current group member.

## Revoke a membership token

<a id="opIddelete-sharegroup-member-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/images/sharegroups/%7B%7BsharegroupId%7D%7D/members/%7B%7BtokenUuid%7D%7D \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/images/sharegroups/{sharegroupId}/members/{tokenUuid}`

Revokes a membership token accepted into a share group. Members with `revoked` status immediately lose access to shared images, and can't deploy them anymore.

- Run the [List share groups](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroups) operation to get the `id` you should use as the `(sharegroupId)` path parameter that identifies an existing share group.

- Run the [List members by share group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-sharegroup-members) operation to get the `token_uuid` for a current group member. After revoking a membership, you can run this operation to check its status.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli image-sharegroups member-delete 123 abc123
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    images:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

## Update default firewalls

<a id="opIdput-firewall-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/networking/firewalls/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "default_firewall_ids": {
      "linode": 100,
      "nodebalancer": 101,
      "public_interface": 200,
      "vpc_interface": 200
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /{apiVersion}/networking/firewalls/settings`

__Beta__ You can update or add a default firewall to:

- Linodes using legacy config profile interfaces

- Linode VPC interfaces and Linode public interfaces

- NodeBalancers

If a firewall isn't provided during service creation, a default firewall is assigned, unless you have opted out of firewall protection.

> 📘
>
> Default firewalls on Linodes with Linode interfaces are applied to the interfaces, not the Linode itself.
>
> Default firewalls on Linodes with legacy configuration profile interfaces are applied directly to the Linode, not its interfaces.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli firewalls firewall-settings-update \
  --default_firewall_ids.vpc_interface 1 \
  --default_firewall_ids.public_interface 2 \
  --default_firewall_ids.nodebalancer 3 \
  --default_firewall_ids.linode 5
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    account:read_write
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-firewall-settings">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

```json
{
  "default_firewall_ids": {
    "linode": 100,
    "nodebalancer": 101,
    "public_interface": 200,
    "vpc_interface": 200
  }
}
```

## Get a firewall template

<a id="opIdget-firewall-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/networking/firewalls/templates/%7B%7Bslug%7D%7D \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/networking/firewalls/templates/{slug}`

__Beta__ Gets a `vpc` or `public` firewall template you can use with Linode VPC and public interfaces. Firewall templates come with some protection rules already configured.

The public interface's firewall template allows for login with SSH, and regular networking control data. You should further strengthen these rules by limiting the allowed IPv4 and IPv6 ranges.

The VPC interface's firewall template allows for login with SSH, regular networking control data, and inbound traffic from the VPC address space. You should further strengthen these rules by limiting the allowed IPv4 and IPv6 ranges.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli firewalls template-view vpc
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    firewall:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-firewall-template">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

|slug|path|string|true|__Enum__ The firewall template type, available for either `vpc` or `public` interfaces.|

<h1 id="akamai-linode-api-devices">Devices</h1>

## List firewall devices

<a id="opIdget-firewall-devices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/networking/firewalls/%7B%7BfirewallId%7D%7D/devices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /{apiVersion}/networking/firewalls/{firewallId}/devices`

Returns a paginated list of a firewall's devices. A firewall device assigns a firewall to a service (referred to as the device's `entity`).


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli firewalls devices-list 123
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- __OAuth scopes__.

    ```
    firewall:read_only
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth)

<a href="https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-firewall-devices">See documentation for this operation in Akamai's Linode API</a>

## Create a firewall device

<a id="opIdpost-firewall-device"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/networking/firewalls/%7B%7BfirewallId%7D%7D/devices \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": 123,
    "type": "linode"
  }'
```

`POST /{apiVersion}/networking/firewalls/{firewallId}/devices`

Creates a firewall device, which assigns a firewall to a service (referred to as the device's `entity`) and applies the firewall's rules to the device.

- Currently, devices with `linode`, `linode_interface`, and `nodebalancer` entity types are accepted.
  - The `linode` type is not allowed for Linodes using Linode interfaces.
  - The `linode_interface` type is not allowed for legacy config interfaces. For VPC and public legacy config profile interfaces, the firewall is applied through the `linode` device.

- Firewalls only apply to inbound TCP traffic to NodeBalancers.

- A firewall can be assigned to multiple services at a time.

- A service can have one assigned firewall at a time.

- Assigned Linodes must not have any ongoing live migrations.

- A `firewall_device_add` event is generated when the firewall device is added successfully.


<<LB>>

---


- __CLI__.

    ```
    linode-cli firewalls device-create 123 \
  --id 456 \
  --type "linode"
    ```

    [Learn more...](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

## Delete a firewall device

<a id="opIddelete-firewall-device"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.linode.com/v4/%7B%7BapiVersion%7D%7D/networking/firewalls/%7B%7BfirewallId%7D%7D/devices/%7B%7BdeviceId%7D%7D \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /{apiVersion}/networking/firewalls/{firewallId}/devices/{deviceId}`

Removes a Firewall Device, which removes a Firewall from the service it was assigned to by the Device. This removes all of the Firewall's Rules from the service. If any other Firewalls have been assigned to the service, then those Rules remain in effect.

- Assigned Linodes must not have any ongoing live migrations.

- A `firewall_device_remove` Event is generated when the Firewall Device is removed successfully.
